the development of a novel speckled tracking technique to measure the changes in the aortic fractional shortening (AFC) during the cardiac systole in MCDA twins.
the development and validation of a new method to assess aortic distensibility.
the study of the cardiovascular system and the effects of TTTS on the heart and blood vessels of the twins.

there is no evidence to support the hypothesis that there are differences in aortic distensibility between MCDA pregnancies with and without TTFS.
the use of AFAC as a surrogate of intertwin pulse‐pressure differences is a novel, non‐invasive method to identify the presence of TTTS in MCDA twins.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the aortic distensibility in MCDA twins is a surrogate for the intertwin pulse pressures.
we have developed a new non‐invasive ultrasound‐based method to assess the cardiac function of fetuses in utero.
we have shown that the donor twin in TTTS is more hypovolemic than its co‐twin and that the recipient twin has a higher afterload.
The main takeaway from our work is that
AFAC is a surrogate for inter‐twin pulse pressure difference (PPD) in MCDA twin gestations.
AFAC is an excellent surrogate for pulse pressure and can be used to identify twins with increased intertwin differences, as well as twins at increased risk of developing TTTS.
AFAC can be used to quantify the intertwin pulse‐pressure differences in MCDA twins and may be a surrogate for TTTS.
